title: Power Platform Environments - Simply Explained
description:
Every licensed user can build in the default environment, yet Microsoft says not to run production work there. This episode explains Power Platform environments, types, Dataverse, roles and governance in plain words for makers and admins. You will know which environment to build in and why.
In this episode
00:00 – Why the default environment is a trap00:25 – What an environment actually is02:30 – Environment types04:53 – Dataverse: one database per environment05:56 – Roles and access07:55 – Environment groups and Managed Environments10:00 – ALM, solutions and data policies13:40 – Best practices
Key takeaways
An app can only reach data sources in its own environment, so many broken connections are boundaries rather than bugs.Use the default environment only for personal experiments, build in developer or sandbox environments and ship managed solutions to production.Maker rights and data access are separate, and data policies, environment groups and Managed Environments add tenant-wide guardrails.
Worth quoting
“An app can only connect to data sources that live in the same environment. If you build an app in one environment and the data sits in another, the app can't see it.” – Mirko Peters (01:59)
“Being allowed to build in an environment isn't the same as being allowed to read its data, and those are two separate doors.” – Mirko Peters (06:16)
Explore more on M365.FM
Episode page: the full episode with chapters, quotes, key takeaways and FAQPower Platform – the platform whose environments, roles, groups and data policies this episode explainsDataverse – each environment holds at most one Dataverse database, and it never holds twoConnector – the bridge an app uses to reach services, sorted into groups by data policiesData loss prevention (DLP) – data policies that group connectors as business, non-business or blocked to stop leaksModel-driven app – an app type that leans on the Dataverse tables of its own environmentRelated episode: Power Platform Copilot Integration - Simply Explained
